conserved_row.complete_before_row: 1.2 This proves the forward direction for every signed torus knot as well. Reflection carries its oriented meridian to the inverse positive meridian of the reflected knot: it preserves the carried knot orientation and reverses the ambient normal-plane orientation. It carries its preferred longitude to the preferred longitude, because the degree along the knot remains one and its exterior homology class remains zero; uniqueness in [F3] excludes any meridian shift. Composition of representations with this exterior diffeomorphism therefore identifies the peripheral loci by $(M,L)\mapsto(M^{-1},L)$, preserving irreducibility and all closure dimensions. Their reduced curve equations differ by that Laurent substitution and a unit. Reversing the knot orientation instead inverts both peripheral generators and gives $(M,L)\mapsto(M^{-1},L^{-1})$. These invertible integral changes of exponents preserve containment in an affine line. Finally swapping the two complex coordinates of the standard $S^3$ interchanges the two torus parameters and preserves ambient orientation; the radial torus parameter may be changed by a smooth radial isotopy. Thus, using the mirror and orientation conventions in [F1], every coprime torus knot reduces to the positive case, or to the unknot if one parameter has absolute value one. In the latter case the actual sine-cosine circle isotopy and ambient extension in the unit-slope supplier [F1] give the unknot, with its countable-choice hypothesis supplied by full AC. This is a proof of thinness for mirrors, not an assertion that the displayed positive formula applies unchanged to a negative knot. [F1, F3, step 1.1, construct, algebra]
